name: HR-VISPR
description: Recent advances in AI-powered surveillance have inten-sified concerns over the collection and processing of sensitive personal data. In response, research has increasingly focused on privacy-by-design solutions, raising the need for objective techniques to evaluate privacy protection. This paper presents a comprehensive framework for evaluating visual privacy-protection methods across three dimensions: privacy, utility, and practicality. In addition, it introduces HR-VISPR, a publicly available11https://github.com/Sara-Esam/HR-VISPR human-centric dataset with biometric, soft-biometric, and non-biometric labels to train an interpretable privacy metric. We evaluate 11 privacy protection methods, ranging from conventional techniques to advanced deep-learning methods, through the proposed framework.
